signal: EliseAI raised a $250M Series E at a $2.2B valuation and crossed $100M ARR, growing past 300 employees

email.body1:
Jack, saw EliseAI close its $250M Series E at a $2.2B valuation and cross $100M ARR.

Growing that fast usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for EliseAI off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jack, quick follow-up for EliseAI.

Post-raise, the number tends to climb faster than headcount can, and most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to book to hit it. The gap shows up late, and then it is a scramble to recover the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings EliseAI needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jack, last bit of proof for EliseAI.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how EliseAI's reply rate likely compares to other high-growth startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jack, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The post-raise stretch is its own kind of busy, and timing is everything.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to EliseAI either way.
